scores.worst_problem: The keyword LIST has nothing to do with the promised deliverable (a concession script and a buydown payment comparison), so the ask feels arbitrary and forgettable at the exact moment friction matters most.
scores.fix: Change the keyword to one that names the payoff — BUYDOWN or CONCESSION — and tighten the last loop from the vague 'I keep a list for this' to something that previews the actual asset, e.g. 'The exact line to write'.

points.title: Supply Flipped
body: Texas has more homes sitting on the market than any point in over a decade.
That is not a crash. It is just competition, and for once it is not aimed at you.

points.title: The Price Cut Trap
body: Most cuts you see are just an overpriced home walking back to normal.
You are not getting a deal. You are watching a correction and calling it one.

points.title: Ask For The Rate
body: A seller paying down your rate moves your money more than a small price drop does.
Same seller cost. Very different outcome for you every single month you own it.

points.title: Watch The Calendar
body: A home listed nine weeks ago has a seller doing math on two housing payments.
That is when concession requests stop being rude and start getting accepted.

points.title: If You Are Selling
body: Your first ten days pull more real buyers than the next sixty combined.
Price for that window. Chasing the market down with cuts is how homes go stale.

linkedinCaption:
Texas inventory is at its highest level in over a decade. That is competition, not collapse, and buyers finally have room to negotiate.

Most price cuts I see are not deals. They are overpriced listings correcting back to market. The buyer who celebrates a reduction is often just paying what the home was always worth.

The more useful ask is a rate buydown. Same cost to the seller. Very different math for the buyer over the life of the loan.

Timing matters too. A seller nine weeks into a listing is carrying two housing obligations. That is when concession requests get taken seriously.

For sellers, the first ten days do the heavy lifting.

Are you seeing buyers prioritize rate structure over sticker price in your market?
